T: Flowers on the table. Dinner on the way.
D: One busy Valentine's Day in Los Angeles follows a florist and a big tangle of couples falling in and out of love.
P: Serve dessert when Reed's flower shop closes for the night.
S: Strawberries dipped in dark chocolate and chopped pistachios

Fresh strawberries dipped in dark chocolate, rolled in crushed pistachios and freeze-dried raspberry, then drizzled with white chocolate. Wash and dry 500g strawberries completely, keeping the stalks on. Melt 150g dark chocolate in a bowl over simmering water. Dip each berry two-thirds of the way in, let the excess drip off and roll the base in 50g finely chopped pistachios. Lay on baking paper. Melt 50g white chocolate and drizzle over with a fork, then dust with a pinch of crushed freeze-dried raspberry. Chill 20 minutes until set.
Reed's flower shop goat's cheese toasts
Sourdough hearts with whipped goat's cheese and chilli honey

Heart-shaped sourdough toasts with whipped goat's cheese, hot honey, thyme and edible flowers, pretty enough for the shop counter. Cut 8 hearts from 8 slices sourdough, brush with olive oil and toast at 190C for 8 minutes until crisp. Whip 150g soft goat's cheese with 50g cream cheese until smooth. Warm 3 tbsp honey with 1/2 tsp chilli flakes. Spread the toasts with the cheese, drizzle with hot honey, scatter with thyme leaves and finish with a few edible flowers or pomegranate seeds.
M: Sirloin steaks with garlic butter and crisp smashed potatoes

Pan-seared sirloin basted in garlic thyme butter, with crispy smashed potatoes, buttered greens and a red wine jus. Boil 800g baby potatoes for 15 minutes, drain, smash flat on a tray, drizzle with oil and roast at 220C for 30 minutes. Season 4 sirloin steaks and sear in a hot pan for 3 minutes a side. Add 50g butter, 2 crushed garlic cloves and thyme and baste for 1 minute. Rest the steaks. Add 150ml red wine and 150ml beef stock to the pan and reduce by half. Sauté 300g green beans in butter.
W: Red velvet cupcakes with cream cheese frosting

Soft red velvet cupcakes with a hint of cocoa and buttermilk, topped with tangy cream cheese icing and red velvet crumbs. Beat 115g butter with 200g caster sugar, add 2 eggs, then 1 tsp vanilla and 1 tsp red colouring paste. Fold in 200g plain flour, 2 tbsp cocoa, 1 tsp bicarb and 160ml buttermilk mixed with 1 tsp vinegar. Divide between 12 cases and bake at 180C for 20 minutes. Cool. Beat 200g cream cheese, 60g butter and 250g icing sugar and pipe on. Crumble one cupcake over the rest.
K: Sparkling rosé with grapefruit juice, raspberries and rosemary

Sparkling rosé with fresh raspberries, a splash of pink grapefruit and a rosemary sprig. Pink lemonade with the same garnish for non-drinkers. Drop 3 raspberries into each of 4 flutes. Add 30ml pink grapefruit juice to each glass. Slowly top with chilled sparkling rosé, about 120ml per glass. Rub a small rosemary sprig between your hands and add one to each glass. For anyone not drinking, use pink lemonade instead of rosé.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes until just tender, drain, smash flat on a tray, drizzle with oil and roast at 220C.

veg.n: Valentine's portobello steaks with garlic butter
veg.make_ahead: Boil the potatoes up to 1 day ahead and keep in the fridge; sear the mushrooms and make the sauce on the night

steps.text: Boil the potatoes until just tender, drain, smash flat on a tray, drizzle with half the oil and roast at 220C.
Season the portobellos and sear in the rest of the oil, gill side up first, until browned on both sides.
Add most of the butter, the garlic and thyme and baste. Lift out the mushrooms.
Add the wine and stock to the pan and reduce by half.
Saute the beans in the remaining butter. Serve with the mushrooms and potatoes.
